turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in class. Who decided that?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry.
Okay. Was Owen heard before it went in?
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Read it yourself.
Turn it toward me. Kids draft in other places and paste it in. You still haven't said whether Owen was heard before that zero went in.
If he drafted somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you.
Fine. Whatever happens next, nothing goes on his record and nothing happens in front of his class. And for the third time, was Owen heard before that zero went in?
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. It is not in Hamlet. Search the play yourself.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote things, Hale. Show me that line in his essay and give me the play.

You mentioned his December 1 deadline. Under 4.4 he can do a supervised rewrite this Thursday, private, in my room. I will mark it by Monday, so the new mark replaces the zero before December 1, and nothing goes on his record. I will put the dates in writing tonight.

I never said December 1, but it's the right date. To put this behind him, Owen will do the rewrite Thursday, private, in your room, and its mark replaces the zero. Tonight's email says that, says nothing goes on his record, and says who decided on the zero before anyone spoke to him.
He'll be there Thursday. Send the email.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today that Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite in your room this Thursday, that you will mark it by Monday, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still want a written account of who decided on the zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before it was entered. I expect that in writing tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position; she agreed to the private supervised rewrite on Thursday with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants a written account of who decided on the zero and whether Owen was heard first, which is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: showing the version history with its exact times and letting her read it, then answering her pasted-from-elsewhere defence with an offer to check that file's dates, because it was specific, dated, tied to Owen's work and checkable.
What cost ground: you never answered whether Owen was heard before the zero, though she asked three times, and you said she had raised the December 1 deadline when she had not, which made her trust your other facts a little less.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history landed on a late night in October, the night before the essay was due, about as close as evidence could come, and that proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she first asked whether Owen was heard before the zero went in, answer it plainly in one sentence before you show the version history, so the evidence lands without an open procedural question beside it.
